etymology: English: assignment by lot - the oldest anti-corruption technology in the book, older than the book.
effect: Takes the choice of judge, panel, or jury out of the hands of the party who benefits from it.
costs: A docket that is less convenient, and a schedule nobody can optimise.
failure: The carve-out for complex cases, which is where the shopping goes to live.
tell: A docket you cannot predict from outside

confused_with.tell: Judge shopping chooses the courtroom; the random draw removes the choice that made the courtroom worth choosing.

senses: Assignment by lot: cases, judges, panels, and sometimes citizens are drawn rather than chosen. It is the same principle as the jury, and it works by making the choice uninteresting.

It works because randomness removes the negotiation. Any assignment system that can be gamed will be gamed, so the fix is not a better rule about who chooses - it is the removal of the choice, which is also why the carve-outs matter more than the rule.
example: *"The division was redrawn to assign cases by **random draw**, and the filing that had gone to one courthouse for six years started going to nine."*
